triage.note: Found by the T3 normalization spike, not by a failing case -- no check anywhere in the eval set asserted anything about normalized_text itself, so an entire class of normalization defect (machine metadata leaking into the human-readable text) was invisible until segmentation existed to carry it into an item span. Backs the new INV-S5; the norm_contains/norm_not_contains check types were added to the adapter for it. Invariant added first, watched red, then fixed (specs/decisions/ADR-006-normalization-rulings.md).

provenance: AAPL FY2025 10-K (iXBRL), EDGAR accession 0000320193-25-000079 -- the same fixture as aapl-2025-structure/content, reused because the defect is a property of the iXBRL format era, not of a corrupted input (fixture reuse precedent: malformed-html reuses premier-pacific-2016). MEASURED with the throwaway T3 spike normalizer (stdlib html.parser per ADR-003, block tags -> newline, inline tags -> nothing, script/style skipped, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed) run against the committed fixture on 2026-08-15: the iXBRL context header is emitted as visible text. Raw fixture has <ix:header> spanning bytes 1,202-86,807 (85.6 KB, containing <ix:hidden> at 1,213-5,007); its text content -- the character data of <xbrldi:explicitMember>, <ix:nonNumeric> and friends -- normalizes to a ~12,880-char run of concatenated XBRL context junk at the very head of normalized_text, e.g. 'false2025FY0000320193P1YP1Yhttp://fasb.org/us-gaap/2025#LongTermDebtNoncurrent...' and '...0000320193us-gaap:OperatingSegmentsMemberaapl:RestOfAsiaPacificSegmentMember2022-09-25...'. Occurrence counts in that naive normalized_text (220,607 chars total): 'us-gaap:' 144x (first at offset 927, last at 12,425), 'OperatingSegmentsMember' 15x, 'http://fasb.org/us-gaap/2025#' present in the opening run; the human-readable document begins only after that, at 'UNITED STATES / SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION / Washington, D.C. 20549 / FORM 10-K'. Raw-file counts differ and are NOT what this case asserts ('us-gaap:' occurs 1,303x in the raw bytes, almost all as attribute values, which the parser never emits as text) -- the three norm_not_contains checks are deliberately phrased against strings that a human reading the filing never sees, so a legitimate 10-K body can never trip them. Same defect confirmed on the second iXBRL deep-tier fixture jpm-2024 and it is far worse there: </ix:header> at raw byte 1,204,900, 'us-gaap:' 2,889x in normalized_text with the last at offset 221,339 of 1,435,196 -- i.e. 15.4% of the normalized document is XBRL metadata before a single readable word. Not asserted on jpm here (one case, one input path); the fix is shared, and jpm-2024-structure's existing checks cover the outcome. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: offsets are the contract's unit of provenance (INV-S2), so a 12.9K / 221K junk prefix displaces every offset in the document; the layer-8 coverage-ratio and gap validators would measure against a denominator that is 15% garbage; and the frontend's normalized_text view would open on metadata. THE THREE POSITIVE CHECKS ARE LOAD-BEARING and were chosen to bound an over-aggressive fix at both ends: a normalizer that simply dropped everything before the cover page, or dropped every element it did not recognize, would satisfy all three norm_not_contains checks while destroying the document -- so 'SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION' pins the text immediately AFTER the header block (i.e. the cut must land exactly there, not later), 'Company Background' pins Item 1 body text (an existing verified anchor from aapl-2025-content), and 'San Jose, California' pins the auditor's report deep inside Item 8 near the end of the document (also an existing verified anchor from aapl-2025-content). All three were confirmed present in the naive spike output before this case was written, so they discriminate the fix, not the fixture. Authored 2026-08-15 at T3; watched red first (0/6 checks -- extract_items raised NotImplementedError). NOT yet dual-passed by extraction-auditor: pending, per case-authoring step 8. ADDED 2026-08-22 (cold-reviewer finding T3-1, tasks/reviews/gates-2026-08-22.json, HIGH, orchestrator-verified): norm_not_contains('aapl-20250927') -- the raw file's <title> is the source filename, and _Plain emitted it as the first 13 characters of normalized_text ('aapl-20250927\n\nUNITED STATES...'), so this INV-S5 case was green while INV-S5 was violated on its own fixture. The string occurs 1x in normalized_text at origin/main 3c2b8f4 (offset 0) and 0x once <title> joins SKIP_TAGS; it is not a string a reader of the filing sees, so body prose can never trip it. Red line observed before the fix: "normalized_text contains 'aapl-20250927' (1x)". The sibling case html-title-metadata carries the finding's second half (period_end read out of the title) on bac-2006.
